- The bottom-water excess over the surface water (BOT − INT) is near zero from April to September in every year.
- It builds from November or December and peaks in January–February, which is the timing of the longest stratified, anoxic periods.
- It collapses again in March as the stratification breaks down. In the integrated surface samples, the released NH₄ and P then appear as the March–May peaks in @fig-seasonal.

**How robust the seasonal cycle is** (bands and heatmaps in @fig-int-load-season).

- **Sample size.** Before alum, only 2–5 years have paired bottom and surface samples in each summer month (2 in March, 3 in February), so the pre-alum curves rest on very few years. The heatmap shows which: almost all are from 2004–2006, just before Utuhina dosing began, plus single summers in 1993 and 2000. Each later decade has 9–10 years.
- **NH₄ is a consistent seasonal cycle.** In the heatmap it forms a band of colour in nearly every summer: the bottom NH₄ excess exceeds 100 mg/m³ in 5 of the 6 pre-alum years, 9 of 10 in 2006–2016 and all 10 in 2016–2026.
- **DRP and TP are carried by a few years.** In the heatmap they appear as isolated hot spots rather than a band. About half of the summers since 2006 have a short peak above 20 mg/m³: 2008–2010, 2015–2016, 2020–2022 and 2024–2025. The month of the peak varies from year to year, so the monthly medians stay low (0–6 mg/m³) and the upper quartile band is wide, even though release happens in many years.

**Before and after alum.**

- **DRP.** The largest summer DRP excess in each year has a median of about 38 mg/m³ before alum (6 years), against about 19 in 2006–2016 and 26 in 2016–2026.
  - Alum has reduced the P released from the sediment, but less than the monthly medians suggest (7–23 mg/m³ in December–March before alum, 0–6 since).
  - Release still happens in about half of all summers.
- **NH₄** shows no fall. The typical summer peak excess was about 240 mg/m³ before alum, 220 in 2006–2016 and 300 in 2016–2026. It also starts earlier, from November.
- **TP.** The TP excess in 2016–2026 is again larger than in 2006–2016, mostly from the 2020–2022 summers.
- **Reading.** This pattern supports the view that alum caps the release of P from the sediment, but does not reduce the mineralisation of organic matter that supplies N. It has made P release less frequent and smaller, but has not stopped it.

### Stratification strength and internal loading, year by year

```{r}
#| label: fig-strat-vs-load
#| fig-cap: "Summer (December–February) stratification strength from the buoys against the annual maximum bottom-water concentrations (mean of Sites 2 and 5). Labels are hydrological years; colour separates years before full dosing of both streams (≤ 2010) from later years."
#| fig-height: 4.5
sstrat <- bdaily |>
  filter(as.integer(format(date, "%m")) %in% c(12, 1, 2)) |>
  mutate(hy = wq_hy(date)) |>
  group_by(hy) |>
  summarise(n = n(), schmidt = mean(schmidt), strat_days = sum(is_stratified(d_rho)) * 90 / n(),
            anox_days = sum(do_bot < 2, na.rm = TRUE) * 90 / sum(is.finite(do_bot)), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n >= 45)
bmax <- ann |> filter(layer == "BOT", variable %in% c("drp", "nh4")) |>
  group_by(hy, variable) |> summarise(max = mean(max), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = max)
sv <- inner_join(sstrat, bmax, by = "hy") |> mutate(period = ifelse(hy <= 2010, "≤ 2010", "2011–2026"))
sv |>
  pivot_longer(c(drp, nh4), names_to = "var", values_to = "max") |>
  mutate(var = c(drp = "Bottom DRP max (mg/m³)", nh4 = "Bottom NH4 max (mg/m³)")[var]) |>
  pivot_longer(c(schmidt, strat_days), names_to = "x", values_to = "xv") |>
  mutate(x = c(schmidt = "Mean summer Schmidt stability (J/m²)",
               strat_days = "Stratified days, Dec–Feb (scaled to 90)")[x]) |>
  ggplot(aes(xv, max, label = hy, colour = period)) +
  geom_text(size = 2.7) +
  geom_smooth(aes(group = 1), method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_grid(var ~ x, scales = "free") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("≤ 2010" = "grey40", "2011–2026" = "#D55E00")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: strat-load-cor
ct_ <- function(x, y) { k <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(x, y, method = "spearman")); sprintf("ρ = %.2f, p = %.2f", k$estimate, k$p.value) }
r_drp_ss <- ct_(sv$schmidt, sv$drp); r_nh4_ss <- ct_(sv$schmidt, sv$nh4)
r_drp_sd <- ct_(sv$strat_days, sv$drp); r_nh4_sd <- ct_(sv$strat_days, sv$nh4)
```

**Year-to-year links between stratification and bottom concentrations.** These use the `r nrow(sv)` hydrological years with buoy coverage.

- **NH₄:**
  - against mean summer Schmidt stability, `r r_nh4_ss`
  - against stratified days, `r r_nh4_sd`
- **DRP:**
  - against Schmidt stability, `r r_drp_ss`
  - against stratified days, `r r_drp_sd`

**How to read these.**

- The relationships are weakly positive (ρ ≈ 0.4 with Schmidt stability, p ≈ 0.1) and essentially absent for the count of stratified days. Monthly bottom samples catch the peak of each event only by chance, and the strength of stratification matters more than its duration.
- For DRP, the alum era shifts the response downwards. For the same stratification, post-2010 years mostly have lower bottom DRP, with the exceptions of 2015, 2021, 2022 and 2025.
- 2021/22 stands out as high stratification combined with very high DRP, in the year the Puarenga dosing was paused.

### Estimating release rates (fluxes)

Two independent estimates are possible from the monitoring data. Both are compared with the sediment-chamber fluxes measured in the lake by Burger et al. (2007) and with the values in the model's `aed.nml`.

**1. Hypolimnetic accumulation (NH₄, DRP, TP).**

- **Which samples are used.** Pairs of consecutive monthly samples at the same site when the CTD casts show the lake stratified on both dates.
- **Hypolimnetic mass.** The mean of the HYP and BOT samples multiplied by the volume below the thermocline (from the hypsograph, using the mean thermocline depth of the two casts).
- **Flux.** The change in that mass divided by the time between samples and by the sediment area below the thermocline.
- **These are lower bounds.** The lake mixes partially between monthly samples, so some released mass is lost upward. Positive intervals are summarised below.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-hyp-flux
#| tbl-cap: "Hypolimnetic accumulation fluxes (mg/m²/d) from consecutive stratified CTD and chemistry sampling dates, 2003–2026. n is the number of sample pairs; positive pairs are those where the hypolimnetic mass increased."
hflux |>
  group_by(Variable = c(nh4 = "NH4-N", drp = "DRP", tp = "TP")[variable]) |>
  summarise(`Pairs (n)` = n(), `Positive` = sum(flux > 0),
            `Median of positive` = median(flux[flux > 0]),
            `75th pct of positive` = quantile(flux[flux > 0], .75),
            `Max` = max(flux),
            `Thermocline (m)` = median(z_th), `Mean hypolimnion thickness (m)` = median(h_mean),
            `Interval (d)` = median(days)) |>
  kable(digits = 1)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-hyp-flux
#| fig-cap: "Hypolimnetic accumulation fluxes for each pair of stratified sampling dates, against mean bottom temperature. Open symbols are negative (net loss, usually partial mixing between samples)."
#| fig-height: 4
hflux |>
  mutate(variable = factor(c(nh4 = "NH4-N", drp = "DRP", tp = "TP")[variable], c("NH4-N", "DRP", "TP")),
         sign = ifelse(flux > 0, "gain", "loss")) |>
  ggplot(aes(t_bot, flux, colour = site, shape = sign)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(gain = 16, loss = 1)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_site) +
  labs(x = "Bottom temperature (°C)", y = "Flux (mg/m²/d)", colour = NULL, shape = NULL)
```

**2. Hypolimnetic oxygen depletion (from the buoys).**

- **Which periods are used.** Each buoy-recorded stratified period (at least 7 days) that starts with bottom DO above 2 g/m³.
- **Volumetric rate.** A regression of daily bottom DO against time, up to the point where DO first falls below 1 g/m³.
- **Areal hypolimnetic oxygen demand (AHOD).** The volumetric rate multiplied by the mean hypolimnion thickness below the median thermocline depth of the period.
- **What it measures.** AHOD is a measure of total sediment and hypolimnetic oxygen demand. It is directly comparable with chamber sediment oxygen demand (SOD).

```{r}
#| label: fig-hod
#| fig-cap: "Hypolimnetic oxygen depletion in buoy-recorded stratified periods. Left: volumetric rate against mean bottom temperature, with an exponential (θ) fit. Right: areal hypolimnetic oxygen demand (AHOD) by year, with the interquartile range of the Burger et al. (2007) light-chamber SOD (grey band)."
#| fig-height: 4
hod_ok <- hod |> filter(rate > 0, r2 >= 0.5)
th_fit <- lm(log(rate) ~ I(t_bot - 20), data = hod_ok)
theta <- exp(coef(th_fit)[2]); r20 <- exp(coef(th_fit)[1])
h1 <- ggplot(hod_ok, aes(t_bot, rate)) + geom_point() +
  geom_line(data = tibble::tibble(t_bot = seq(10, 23, 0.1)) |> mutate(rate = r20 * theta^(t_bot - 20)),
            colour = "#D55E00") +
  labs(x = "Mean bottom temperature (°C)", y = "DO decline (g/m³/d)")
h2 <- ggplot(hod_ok, aes(start, ahod)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = quantile(burger$sod_g_m2_d[burger$chamber == "light"], .25),
           ymax = quantile(burger$sod_g_m2_d[burger$chamber == "light"], .75), fill = "grey85") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = t_bot)) + scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "C") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "AHOD (g O₂/m²/d)", colour = "T bottom (°C)")
h1 + h2
```

```{r}
#| label: flux-numbers
ahod_med <- median(hod_ok$ahod); ahod_iqr <- quantile(hod_ok$ahod, c(.25, .75))
rate_med <- median(hod_ok$rate)
# Redfield mineralisation: 138 mol O2 : 16 mol N : 1 mol P
gN_per_gO2 <- 16 * 14.007 / (138 * 31.998); gP_per_gO2 <- 30.974 / (138 * 31.998)
pos <- function(v) median(hflux$flux[hflux$variable == v & hflux$flux > 0])
```

**Oxygen depletion results.**

- Across `r nrow(hod_ok)` well-fitted stratified periods (r² ≥ 0.5), bottom DO fell at a median `r sprintf("%.2f", rate_med)` g/m³/d.
- The median AHOD is **`r sprintf("%.1f", ahod_med)` g O₂/m²/d** (interquartile range `r sprintf("%.1f–%.1f", ahod_iqr[1], ahod_iqr[2])`).
- The depletion rate rises with bottom temperature, with θ ≈ `r sprintf("%.3f", theta)` per °C. That is about `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * (theta^5 - 1))` % faster at 20 °C than at 15 °C. This is one mechanism by which warmer summers strengthen internal loading.
- The AHOD values sit within the chamber SOD range of Burger et al. (2007), 0.3–4.0 g O₂/m²/d in the light chambers. They are towards the upper part of it, which is expected, because AHOD also includes oxygen demand in the water column below the thermocline.

**Converting oxygen demand to nutrient release.** If the oxygen demand were all due to the mineralisation of Redfield organic matter (O₂:N:P = 138:16:1 by mole), the median AHOD would correspond to:

- about **`r sprintf("%.0f", ahod_med * 1000 * gN_per_gO2)` mg N/m²/d**
- about **`r sprintf("%.1f", ahod_med * 1000 * gP_per_gO2)` mg P/m²/d**

This is an upper-bound-type estimate for N. For P it is an estimate of mineralisation only. It excludes P released when iron oxides are reduced, which can be larger, and it excludes the P bound by alum.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-flux-compare
#| tbl-cap: "Comparison of internal-load flux estimates for Lake Rotorua (mg/m²/d, O₂ in g/m²/d). Chamber values are the range of the light-chamber means of Burger et al. (2007), 2003–2004, at 7–20 m depth. The aed.nml values are the current model settings (three sediment zones)."
bl <- burger |> filter(chamber == "light")
fmt_r <- function(x, d = 0) paste(formatC(min(x), format = "f", digits = d), "–", formatC(max(x), format = "f", digits = d))
tibble::tribble(
  ~Method, ~`NH4-N`, ~`DRP / SRP`, ~`O2 demand`,
  "Hypolimnetic accumulation, this study (median of positive intervals; lower bound)",
    sprintf("%.0f", pos("nh4")), sprintf("%.1f", pos("drp")), "–",
  "Hypolimnetic accumulation, 75th percentile / max",
    sprintf("%.0f / %.0f", quantile(hflux$flux[hflux$variable == "nh4" & hflux$flux > 0], .75), max(hflux$flux[hflux$variable == "nh4"])),
    sprintf("%.1f / %.1f", quantile(hflux$flux[hflux$variable == "drp" & hflux$flux > 0], .75), max(hflux$flux[hflux$variable == "drp"])), "–",
  "Oxygen depletion (AHOD), buoys, median",
    sprintf("%.0f (Redfield)", ahod_med * 1000 * gN_per_gO2), sprintf("%.1f (Redfield)", ahod_med * 1000 * gP_per_gO2),
    sprintf("%.1f", ahod_med),
  "Burger et al. 2007 chambers (light, 7–20 m)",
    paste(fmt_r(bl$nh4_phase2_mg_m2_d), "(phase 2);", fmt_r(bl$nh4_phase1_mg_m2_d), "(phase 1)"),
    fmt_r(bl$srp_mg_m2_d, 1), fmt_r(bl$sod_g_m2_d, 2),
  "Model aed.nml (fsed_amm, fsed_frp, fsed_oxy; zones 1–3)",
    paste(sprintf("%.0f", c(6.654, 2.408, 0.616) * 14.007), collapse = ", "),
    paste(sprintf("%.1f", c(0.0602, 0.0657, 0.0254) * 30.974), collapse = ", "),
    paste(sprintf("%.2f", c(30.1, 30.1, 23.33) * 31.998 / 1000), collapse = ", ")
) |> kable()
```

**How the estimates compare.**

- **NH₄.**
  - The accumulation estimates (median about 25 mg N/m²/d, up to about 80) are at the low end of the chamber rates (33–224 mg N/m²/d in the secondary phase).
  - The oxygen-demand-based estimate (about 78 mg N/m²/d) sits within them.
  - Together they put summer NH₄ release in Rotorua at roughly **25–100 mg N/m²/d**, so the model's zone-1 value (about 93 mg N/m²/d) is plausible.
  - The two deeper zones (34 and 9 mg N/m²/d) look low.
- **DRP.**
  - Accumulation (2004–2024) gives about 2–5 mg P/m²/d (maximum about 8 mg P/m²/d, in 2019/20 and 2020/21).
  - That is at the lower end of the 2003–2004 chamber range (2–86 mg P/m²/d in the light chambers), which was measured before alum dosing.
  - The model's `fsed_frp` (0.8–2 mg P/m²/d) is at or below the lowest observed value. It may be too low unless the model supplies P to the sediment by another route (settling and mineralisation, or the alum-bound pool).
- **Oxygen.** AHOD (interquartile range about 1.0–2.1 g O₂/m²/d) is consistent with the chamber SOD. It is above `fsed_oxy` (0.75–0.96 g O₂/m²/d), but the difference is mostly accounted for by water-column demand below the thermocline.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-internal-annual
#| tbl-cap: "Order-of-magnitude summer internal load: release rate × sediment area below the median summer thermocline × stratified days (December–February, buoy). Low uses the median hypolimnetic accumulation flux and high the 75th percentile (DRP), or the Redfield-equivalent of AHOD (NH4). Compare with the external loads (alum_storm_central)."
a_sed <- hyps_area(hyps, median(bdaily$thermo_depth[as.integer(format(bdaily$date, "%m")) %in% c(12, 1, 2)], na.rm = TRUE))
q_drp <- quantile(hflux$flux[hflux$variable == "drp" & hflux$flux > 0], c(.5, .75))
f_nh4 <- c(pos("nh4"), ahod_med * 1000 * gN_per_gO2)
ext <- loads |> filter(scenario == "alum_storm_central") |> select(hy, ext_tp = tp, ext_tn = tn)
sstrat |>
  inner_join(ext, by = "hy") |>
  transmute(`Hydrological year` = hy, `Stratified days` = round(strat_days),
            `DRP (t P)` = sprintf("%.1f–%.1f", strat_days * a_sed * q_drp[1] / 1e9, strat_days * a_sed * q_drp[2] / 1e9),
            `External TP (t/y)` = round(ext_tp, 1),
            `NH4-N (t N)` = sprintf("%.0f–%.0f", strat_days * a_sed * f_nh4[1] / 1e9, strat_days * a_sed * f_nh4[2] / 1e9),
            `External TN (t/y)` = round(ext_tn)) |>
  kable()
```

**Scaling up to an annual internal load.**

- Sediment area below the median summer thermocline: about `r sprintf("%.0f", a_sed / 1e6)` km².
- Release rates:
  - DRP: `r sprintf("%.1f–%.1f", q_drp[1], q_drp[2])` mg/m²/d
  - NH₄: `r sprintf("%.0f–%.0f", f_nh4[1], f_nh4[2])` mg N/m²/d

**What the scaling suggests.**

- **P.** Each summer's stratified periods release in the order of 3–15 t of DRP in most years, against an external TP load of about 28–60 t/y. It was lowest in the barely stratified 2009/10 (about 1–2 t) and highest in 2021/22 (about 7–16 t).
- **N.** NH₄-N release is in the order of 30–230 t, against an external TN load of 380–815 t/y.

**Limits of these totals.**

- They cover only the stratified bottom layer in December–February.
- They exclude release during mixed periods. Burger et al. (2007) found SRP release largely independent of DO.
- They exclude release from the shallower sediments, which occupy the larger area.

So these are conservative. Earlier whole-lake budgets put internal loading at a substantial share of the total P load. These monitoring-based rates are best treated as the floor of the range the model's sediment fluxes should reproduce.


### Release rates by depth zone {#sec-zone-release}

Burger et al. (2007) measured sediment release in chambers at 7, 14 and 20 m, and a more recent study at 10, 15 and 20 m. The model has separate sediment zones (8–13 m and 13 m to the bed, below the surface zones). This section asks whether the monitoring data can give release rates for separate depth zones too.

- **Oxygen.** The new buoy (from February 2022) measures DO every 0.5 m from 1 to 21 m. In each 1 m layer that stays below the thermocline for a whole stratified period, DO falls at a rate made up of two parts:
  - the demand in the water column;
  - the sediment demand multiplied by the layer's sediment area per unit volume, which comes from the hypsograph and rises with depth.

  Fitting the rates against the sediment area per volume across layers separates the two (Livingstone & Imboden 2009) and would give the sediment demand by depth.
- **Nutrients.** Only the monthly hypolimnion and bottom samples are available below the thermocline (15 and 19 m at Site 2, 18 and 22 m at Site 5). They allow two layers:
  - an upper layer, from the thermocline to midway between the two sampling depths;
  - a lower layer, from there to the bed.

  Accumulation in each layer is measured on stratified sample pairs, as in @tbl-flux-compare.
- Code in `R/zone_release.R`; targets `zone_o2_demand` and `zone_nutrient_flux`.

```{r}
#| label: zone-data
zo <- tr("zone_o2_demand"); znf <- tr("zone_nutrient_flux")
zl <- zo$layers; ze <- zo$events
z_alpha <- tibble(z = 8:20) |> rowwise() |> mutate(alpha = layer_alpha(hyps, z, z + 1)[["alpha"]]) |> ungroup()
zones <- data.frame(zone = c("15 m (12–17 m)", "20 m (17–21 m)"), z0 = c(12, 17), z1 = c(17, 21))
zsum <- zone_summary(zl, zones, "ja_all")
rate_by_z <- zl |> group_by(z) |> summarise(rate = median(rate), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-zone-o2
#| fig-cap: "Oxygen depletion by depth in the stratified periods recorded by the new buoy (February 2022 – February 2026; periods of at least 7 days). (a) DO depletion rate in each 1 m layer below the thermocline; thin lines are individual stratified periods, the thick line the median over periods. (b) Sediment area per unit volume of each 1 m layer, from the hypsograph. If the sediment set the depletion rate in each layer, (a) would rise with depth roughly in proportion to (b)."
#| fig-height: 4.5
za <- ggplot(zl, aes(rate, z_mid)) +
  geom_path(aes(group = event), colour = "#4393C3", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(colour = "#4393C3", size = 1, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_path(data = rate_by_z |> mutate(z_mid = z + 0.5), colour = "#08306B", linewidth = 1.1) +
  scale_y_reverse(limits = c(21, 8)) +
  labs(x = "DO depletion rate (g O₂/m³/d)", y = "Depth (m)", tag = "a")
zb <- ggplot(z_alpha, aes(alpha, z + 0.5)) + geom_path(colour = "grey30") + geom_point(size = 1) +
  scale_y_reverse(limits = c(21, 8)) +
  labs(x = "Sediment area / volume (1/m)", y = NULL, tag = "b")
za + zb + plot_layout(widths = c(1.4, 1))
```

```{r}
#| label: zone-numbers
z_rate_cv <- sd(rate_by_z$rate[rate_by_z$z >= 14]) / mean(rate_by_z$rate[rate_by_z$z >= 14])
a14 <- z_alpha$alpha[z_alpha$z == 14]; a19 <- z_alpha$alpha[z_alpha$z == 19]
ja_neg <- sum(ze$ja < 0); ja_n <- nrow(ze)
zt_med <- median(ze$z_top)
bz <- burger |> group_by(depth_m, chamber) |>
  summarise(sod = median(sod_g_m2_d), nh4 = median(nh4_phase2_mg_m2_d), nh4_1 = median(nh4_phase1_mg_m2_d), srp = median(srp_mg_m2_d), .groups = "drop")
bzv <- function(d, ch, v) { x <- bz[[v]][bz$depth_m == d & bz$chamber == ch]; if (length(x)) x else NA_real_ }
sod_lbl <- function(d) if (is.na(bzv(d, "dark", "sod"))) sprintf("%.2f / – (light only)", bzv(d, "light", "sod")) else sprintf("%.2f / %.2f", bzv(d, "light", "sod"), bzv(d, "dark", "sod"))
bed17 <- hyps_area(hyps, 17) / max(hyps$area)
nfz <- znf |> group_by(variable, layer) |>
  summarise(med = median(flux), q25 = quantile(flux, .25), q75 = quantile(flux, .75), n = n(), pos = mean(flux > 0),
            z0 = median(z0), z1 = median(z1), .groups = "drop")
nfv <- function(v, l, s = "med") nfz[[s]][nfz$variable == v & nfz$layer == l]
zsv <- function(zn, s) { x <- zsum$v[zsum$zone == zn]; c(med = median(x), q25 = unname(quantile(x, .25)), q75 = unname(quantile(x, .75)), n = length(x))[[s]] }
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-zone-release
#| tbl-cap: "Release rates by depth zone. Burger et al. (2007): chamber medians over the four 2003–2004 surveys (light and dark chambers), before alum dosing; NH4 in the secondary (longer-term) phase. Oxygen, this study: the upper bound (all of a layer's DO depletion assigned to its own sediment), median and interquartile range over the buoy's stratified periods 2022–2026, and the lake-wide AHOD (2007–2026). Nutrients, this study: two-layer accumulation from the monthly samples, 2003–2026 (median and interquartile range of the stratified sample pairs; negative values are net losses between samples)."
fq <- function(m, a, b, d = 1) sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f (%.", d, "f to %.", d, "f)"), m, a, b)
tibble::tribble(
  ~Zone, ~`Burger SOD, light / dark (g O₂/m²/d)`, ~`Burger NH4 (mg N/m²/d)`, ~`Burger SRP (mg P/m²/d)`,
  ~`O₂ upper bound, this study (g/m²/d)`, ~`NH4, two-layer (mg N/m²/d)`, ~`DRP, two-layer (mg P/m²/d)`,
  "7–10 m (Burger 7 m)",
    sod_lbl(7), sprintf("%.0f", bzv(7, "light", "nh4")), sprintf("%.1f", bzv(7, "light", "srp")),
    "not measurable (above the thermocline)", "not measurable", "not measurable",
  "14–15 m (Burger 14 m)",
    sod_lbl(14), sprintf("%.0f", bzv(14, "light", "nh4")), sprintf("%.1f", bzv(14, "light", "srp")),
    sprintf("%s, n = %d", fq(zsv("15 m (12–17 m)", "med"), zsv("15 m (12–17 m)", "q25"), zsv("15 m (12–17 m)", "q75"), 2), zsv("15 m (12–17 m)", "n")),
    sprintf("%s, upper layer %.0f–%.0f m", fq(nfv("nh4", "upper"), nfv("nh4", "upper", "q25"), nfv("nh4", "upper", "q75"), 0), nfv("nh4", "upper", "z0"), nfv("nh4", "upper", "z1")),
    fq(nfv("drp", "upper"), nfv("drp", "upper", "q25"), nfv("drp", "upper", "q75")),
  "20 m (Burger 20 m)",
    sod_lbl(20), sprintf("%.0f", bzv(20, "light", "nh4")), sprintf("%.1f", bzv(20, "light", "srp")),
    sprintf("%s, n = %d", fq(zsv("20 m (17–21 m)", "med"), zsv("20 m (17–21 m)", "q25"), zsv("20 m (17–21 m)", "q75"), 2), zsv("20 m (17–21 m)", "n")),
    sprintf("%s, lower layer %.0f m–bed", fq(nfv("nh4", "lower"), nfv("nh4", "lower", "q25"), nfv("nh4", "lower", "q75"), 0), nfv("nh4", "lower", "z0")),
    fq(nfv("drp", "lower"), nfv("drp", "lower", "q25"), nfv("drp", "lower", "q75")),
  "Whole hypolimnion (lake-wide)",
    "–", "–", "–", sprintf("AHOD %.1f", ahod_med), sprintf("%.0f (median of positive intervals)", pos("nh4")), sprintf("%.1f", pos("drp"))
) |> kable()
```

**What the oxygen data show** (@fig-zone-o2).

- **DO falls at about the same rate at every depth below the thermocline.** From 14 m to the bottom the median rate varies by only about `r scales::percent(z_rate_cv, 1)` between layers (about `r sprintf("%.2f", median(rate_by_z$rate[rate_by_z$z >= 14]))` g O₂/m³/d). Over the same depths, the sediment area per unit volume more than doubles (`r sprintf("%.2f", a14)` to `r sprintf("%.2f", a19)` per m).
- **So the bottom layer is mixed faster than its oxygen is used.** The demand of the sediment at each depth is spread through the whole bottom layer within days. This is consistent with the thin bottom layer (mean thickness about 4–6 m) and the frequent partial mixing found in @sec-strat-drivers.
- **The sediment demand cannot be split by depth from these data.** The regression across layers gives unstable results: the fitted sediment demand is negative in `r ja_neg` of `r ja_n` stratified periods. The water-column data constrain only the total demand of the bottom layer, the AHOD.
- **The shallower zones are not reachable.** In the median stratified period, only the layers below about `r zt_med` m stayed below the thermocline throughout. A 7 or 10 m zone sits in the mixed layer for most of the summer. Release there is mixed into the surface water and cannot be measured as a build-up.
- **The upper bound in @tbl-zone-release** assigns all of a layer's depletion to its own sediment. It is about 0.5–0.9 g O₂/m²/d below 12 m. It is higher in the 15 m zone than at 20 m only because the same depletion is divided by a smaller sediment area. It is not evidence that the demand is higher there.

**What the nutrient data show.**

- In the two-layer accumulation, the lower layer accumulates somewhat more NH₄ and DRP per unit sediment area than the upper layer: medians of `r sprintf("%.0f", nfv("nh4", "lower"))` against `r sprintf("%.0f", nfv("nh4", "upper"))` mg N/m²/d, and `r sprintf("%.1f", nfv("drp", "lower"))` against `r sprintf("%.1f", nfv("drp", "upper"))` mg P/m²/d.
- The spread is wide. About a third to half of the sample pairs show a net loss, because mixing between monthly samples removes mass.
- These are net accumulation rates. They are lower bounds of the gross release, and like the lake-wide rates they are well below the chamber rates.

**What the chambers show.** Burger et al. (2007) is the only depth-resolved measurement:

- **SOD:** similar at all three depths (light-chamber medians `r sprintf("%.1f", bzv(7, "light", "sod"))`, `r sprintf("%.1f", bzv(14, "light", "sod"))` and `r sprintf("%.1f", bzv(20, "light", "sod"))` g O₂/m²/d at 7, 14 and 20 m).
- **NH₄ and SRP:** release was much higher at 20 m, in the pre-alum lake.
  - NH₄: `r sprintf("%.0f", bzv(7, "light", "nh4"))`, `r sprintf("%.0f", bzv(14, "light", "nh4"))` and `r sprintf("%.0f", bzv(20, "light", "nh4"))` mg N/m²/d at 7, 14 and 20 m, about twice as high at 20 m.
  - SRP: `r sprintf("%.0f", bzv(7, "light", "srp"))`, `r sprintf("%.0f", bzv(14, "light", "srp"))` and `r sprintf("%.0f", bzv(20, "light", "srp"))` mg P/m²/d, about five times as high at 20 m as at 7 m.

**Implications for the model zones.**

- **Oxygen.** The monitoring cannot tell the model's zone 2 (8–13 m) from zone 1 (13 m to the bed). It constrains only the total demand of the bottom layer (AHOD). The chambers suggest a similar SOD at all depths. Together these support keeping the zone `fsed_oxy` values close to each other, rather than the large mid-depth demand the calibration found (@sec-model-targets).
- **Nutrients.** Both the chambers (strongly) and the two-layer data (weakly) point to higher NH₄ and P release in the deepest zone. That deepest zone (below about 17 m) holds only about `r scales::percent(bed17, 1)` of the lake bed.
- **A zone-resolved measurement would need sediment chambers or cores**, as in Burger et al. (2007) and the recent 10/15/20 m study, not water-column monitoring.


## Sudden changes and events {#sec-events}

### Event definitions {#sec-event-defs}

All events are detected automatically from continuous daily series (functions in `R/wq_synthesis_helpers.R`; targets `met_events` and `buoy_events`).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-event-defs
#| tbl-cap: "Definitions of the events used in this report."
st_thr <- attr(me$storms, "threshold_mm")
tibble::tribble(
  ~Event, ~`Data`, ~Definition, ~`Number detected`,
  "Air heatwave", "ERA5-BC daily mean air temperature, 1976–2026",
    "At least 5 consecutive days above the day-of-year 90th percentile (11-day window, 1991–2020 baseline); gaps of up to 2 days are bridged. This is the Hobday et al. (2016) marine-heatwave definition applied to air temperature.",
    sprintf("%d (%d since 2016)", nrow(me$air_heatwaves), sum(me$air_heatwaves$start >= as.Date("2016-01-01"))),
  "Lake (surface) heatwave", "Buoy daily mean water temperature at ≤ 1.5 m, 2007–2026",
    "Same rule as for air heatwaves, applied to lake surface temperature (cf. Woolway et al. 2021). The climatology uses the whole buoy record, because the record is too short for a 30-year baseline.",
    sprintf("%d", nrow(be$heatwaves)),
  "Heatwave category", "Both",
    "The peak anomaly expressed in multiples of the threshold-minus-climatology difference on that day: 1–2× Moderate, 2–3× Strong, 3–4× Severe, ≥ 4× Extreme (Hobday et al. 2018).",
    "–",
  "Storm (heavy-rain event)", "ERA5-BC daily rainfall, 1976–2026",
    sprintf("The 3-day running rainfall total exceeds its 99th percentile (%.0f mm); exceedances within 3 days of each other are one event. The event magnitude is the largest 3-day total. The peak modelled total inflow (PC10 loads) is reported alongside.", st_thr),
    sprintf("%d (%d since 2016)", nrow(me$storms), sum(me$storms$start >= as.Date("2016-01-01"))),
  "Stratified", "Buoy and CTD profiles",
    "The bottom (≥ 18 m) water is more than 0.2 kg/m³ denser than the surface (≤ 1.5 m) water, from temperature (equal to a 1 °C difference at about 20–21 °C; until November 2026 the definition was a 1 °C difference). Stratified periods are runs of at least 3 such days (gaps of up to 2 days bridged).",
    sprintf("%d periods", nrow(be$stratified)),
  "Bottom anoxia / hypoxia", "Buoy bottom (≥ 18 m) DO",
    "Bottom DO below 2 g/m³ (anoxia) or below 4 g/m³ (hypoxia) for at least 3 days (gaps of up to 2 days bridged).",
    sprintf("%d anoxic periods", nrow(be$anoxia))
) |> kable()
```

### Examples

```{r}
#| label: hw-daily
air_hw <- detect_heatwaves(me$daily$date, me$daily$tair, base_years = 1991:2020)
hw_example <- function(daily, events, from, to, title, ylab) {
  d <- daily |> filter(date >= as.Date(from), date <= as.Date(to))
  ev <- events |> filter(end >= as.Date(from), start <= as.Date(to))
  ggplot(d, aes(date)) +
    geom_rect(data = ev, aes(xmin = start - 0.5, xmax = end + 0.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "#F4A582", alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = thresh, ymax = pmax(temp, thresh)), fill = "#B2182B", alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_line(aes(y = clim), colour = "grey40", linetype = 2) +
    geom_line(aes(y = thresh), colour = "grey40") +
    geom_line(aes(y = temp), colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +
    scale_x_date(date_labels = "%d %b\n%Y") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = ylab, title = title)
}
```

#| label: fig-ex-air-hw

The dashed line is the day-of-year climatology (1991–2020), the solid grey line the 90th-percentile threshold, red fill the exceedance and pink bands the detected heatwave periods. Left: the 21-day summer heatwave of December 2021 – January 2022 (Strong). Right: the August 2022 winter heatwave (Severe), when temperatures were near summer values."
#| fig-height: 3.8
ev_a <- me$air_heatwaves
hw_example(air_hw$daily, ev_a, "2021-11-15", "2022-02-15", "Summer 2021/22", "Air temperature (°C)") +

Right: Christmas 2021 – January 2022 (Strong, 19 days), at the end of the stratified period of summer 2021/22 (at least 70 days; @sec-strat2122)."

```{r}
#| label: fig-ex-storm
#| fig-cap: "Storm examples. Top: ERA5-BC daily rainfall (bars) and 3-day running total (line), with the 99th-percentile 3-day threshold (dashed) and detected storm events (blue bands). Bottom: modelled total inflow to the lake (PC10 loads, all inflows) and daily mean wind speed. Left: late January and February 2023 (the late-January storm and Cyclone Gabrielle). Right: the July 2025 storm sequence, including the second-largest 3-day total in the record."
#| fig-height: 6
storm_example <- function(from, to, title) {
  rr <- me$daily |> arrange(date) |>
    mutate(roll3 = as.numeric(stats::filter(rain_mm, rep(1, 3), sides = 1))) |>
    filter(date >= as.Date(from), date <= as.Date(to))
  ev <- me$storms |> filter(end >= as.Date(from), start <= as.Date(to))
  q <- pflow |> filter(inflow == "All inflows", date >= as.Date(from), date <= as.Date(to))
  p1 <- ggplot(rr, aes(date)) +
    geom_rect(data = ev, aes(xmin = start - 0.5, xmax = end + 0.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "#92C5DE", alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_col(aes(y = rain_mm), fill = "#2166AC", width = 0.8) +
    geom_line(aes(y = roll3), colour = "black") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = st_thr, linetype = 2, colour = "firebrick") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Rain (mm/d; 3-day total)", title = title)
  p2 <- ggplot() +
    geom_line(data = q, aes(date, flow_m3s), colour = "#0072B2") +
    geom_line(data = rr, aes(date, wind * 5), colour = "grey50", linetype = 2) +
    scale_y_continuous(sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / 5, name = "Wind (m/s, dashed)")) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Total inflow (m³/s)")
  p1 / p2 + plot_layout(heights = c(1.4, 1))
}
(storm_example("2023-01-10", "2023-03-10", "Jan – Feb 2023") |
   storm_example("2025-06-20", "2025-08-20", "Jul 2025"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ex-summer
#| fig-cap: "Anatomy of one summer, 2017/18: air temperature (ERA5-BC) with air-heatwave periods, buoy surface and bottom water temperature with lake-heatwave periods, bottom DO with anoxic periods (< 2 g/m³), and daily rainfall with storm events. Shaded bands mark the detected events in each panel."
#| fig-height: 8
from <- as.Date("2017-11-01"); to <- as.Date("2018-03-31")
band <- function(ev, fill) {
  ev <- ev |> filter(end >= from, start <= to)
  geom_rect(data = ev, aes(xmin = start - 0.5, xmax = end + 0.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = fill, alpha = 0.4)
}
w <- \(d) filter(d, date >= from, date <= to)
x_sc <- scale_x_date(limits = c(from, to), date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b %Y")
e1 <- ggplot(w(me$daily), aes(date, tair)) + band(me$air_heatwaves, "#F4A582") +
  geom_line() + x_sc + labs(x = NULL, y = "Air temp (°C)")
e2 <- be$daily |> w() |> select(date, Surface = t_surf, Bottom = t_bot) |>
  pivot_longer(-date) |>
  ggplot(aes(date, value, colour = name)) + band(be$heatwaves, "#D6604D") +
  band(be$stratified, "grey85") + geom_line() + x_sc +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Surface = "#D55E00", Bottom = "#0072B2")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Water temp (°C)", colour = NULL) + theme(legend.position = c(0.9, 0.25))
e3 <- ggplot(w(be$daily), aes(date, do_bot)) + band(be$anoxia, "#B2ABD2") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 2, linetype = 2, colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_line(colour = "purple4") + x_sc + labs(x = NULL, y = "Bottom DO (g/m³)")
e4 <- ggplot(w(me$daily), aes(date, rain_mm)) + band(me$storms, "#92C5DE") +
  geom_col(fill = "#2166AC") + x_sc + labs(x = NULL, y = "Rain (mm/d)")
e1 / e2 / e3 / e4
```

**What the examples show.**

- **Air heatwaves** in Rotorua typically peak 2–6 °C above the climatology and last 1–3 weeks. Since 2016 they have occurred in winter as well as summer. August 2022 was the most intense ("Severe"), with daily means near 15 °C.
- **Lake surface heatwaves** follow air heatwaves combined with light winds.
  - The December 2017 event warmed the surface to about 23 °C while the bottom stayed near 16 °C.
  - It set up a 41-day stratified period, and bottom DO fell from about 10 g/m³ to below 2 g/m³ in about four weeks.
- **Mixing ends the anoxia.** Mixing in late December, then the storm of early January 2018 (149 mm in 3 days, daily mean wind up to 14 m/s), reoxygenated the bottom water. A hot spell then re-stratified the lake: a second lake heatwave in late January brought the surface to 24.7 °C, and anoxia returned within two weeks.
- **Storms** are mostly 2–4-day events, and the modelled total inflow responds within a day.
  - **Late January 2023:** inflow peaked at 83 m³/s and stayed above about 25 m³/s for three weeks.
  - **Cyclone Gabrielle:** more rain (229 mm in 3 days), and the windiest of the large storms (daily mean wind about 15 m/s), but a smaller modelled inflow peak (about 34 m³/s).
  - **The July 2025 sequence:** three storms in five weeks, ending with the second-largest 3-day total on record (285 mm) and an inflow peak of about 60 m³/s.


### Detected change points

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cps
#| tbl-cap: "Change points in the mean of deseasonalised monthly series (binary segmentation, ≥ 24-month segments), integrated samples. Values are segment means in mg/m³ (Secchi in m)."
cps |>
  filter(layer == "INT") |>
  mutate(variable = var_lab[variable], cp = format(cp_date, "%b %Y"),
         across(c(mean_before, mean_after, delta), \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
  select(Variable = variable, Site = site, `Change at` = cp, Before = mean_before,
         After = mean_after, Change = delta) |>
  arrange(Variable, Site) |>
  kable()
```

**The change points group into a few episodes.**

1. **1996–2002.** TN, chl-a and organic N increase. This is the late-1990s deterioration that led to the 2000s blooms.
2. **2007–2010.** TP, DRP and particulate P fall, and TN, chl-a and organic N fall about a year later. This follows the start of dosing at Utuhina in 2006 and Puarenga in 2010.
3. **2011.** A step up in NOx at both sites, with a similar step in several streams in April 2011. It may be partly analytical.
4. **2019–2021.** A step up in TP (Jun–Nov 2020) and DRP (2019–2021), reversed in late 2022. This aligns with the Puarenga dosing pause.
5. **2015 and 2021–2023.** Steps up in TN and NH₄ (bottom NH₄ from Jan 2015; INT NH₄ Apr 2021; TN Jul 2021 and Feb 2023).

### Event timeline

```{r}
#| label: fig-timeline
#| fig-cap: "Lake response (top: monthly mean integrated TP and bottom DRP, both sites) against events (bottom): ERA5-BC storms (3-day rain > 99th percentile; size = total), air heatwaves, lake heatwaves, buoy anoxic periods and alum dosing gaps."
#| fig-height: 8
x0 <- as.Date("2003-01-01")
resp <- lw |>
  filter(date >= x0, (layer == "INT" & variable == "tp") | (layer == "BOT" & variable == "drp")) |>
  mutate(m = as.Date(format(date, "%Y-%m-01")),
         series = ifelse(variable == "tp", "INT TP", "BOT DRP")) |>
  group_by(series, m) |> summarise(value = mean(value), .groups = "drop")
pt <- ggplot(resp, aes(m, value, colour = series)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point(size = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("INT TP" = "#009E73", "BOT DRP" = "#CC79A7")) +
  scale_x_date(limits = c(x0, as.Date("2026-07-01")), date_breaks = "2 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "mg/m³", colour = NULL) + theme(legend.position = "top")
seg <- bind_rows(
  me$air_heatwaves |> transmute(start, end, type = "Air heatwave"),
  be$heatwaves |> transmute(start, end, type = "Lake heatwave"),
  be$anoxia |> transmute(start, end, type = "Bottom anoxia (buoy)"),
  pua_pause |> transmute(start, end, type = "Puarenga dosing paused")
) |> filter(end >= x0)
st <- me$storms |> filter(peak_date >= x0)
pe <- ggplot() +
  geom_segment(data = seg, aes(x = start, xend = end + 3, y = type, yend = type, colour = type),
               linewidth = 5) +
  geom_point(data = st, aes(peak_date, "Storm (3-day rain)", size = total_mm),
             colour = "#0072B2", alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Air heatwave" = "orange", "Lake heatwave" = "firebrick",
                                 "Bottom anoxia (buoy)" = "purple",
                                 "Puarenga dosing paused" = "grey40"), guide = "none") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 6) +
  scale_x_date(limits = c(x0, as.Date("2026-07-01")), date_breaks = "2 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, size = "Rain (mm)")
pt / pe + plot_layout(heights = c(1.3, 1))
```

### Storm events and the lake response

```{r}
#| label: tbl-storms
#| tbl-cap: "Largest 3-day rainfall events in the bias-corrected ERA5 record since 2000, with the modelled peak total inflow (PC10 loads) within ±3 days."
allin <- pflow |> filter(inflow == "All inflows")
me$storms |>
  filter(peak_date >= as.Date("2000-01-01")) |>
  arrange(desc(total_mm)) |> head(15) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(peak_q = max(allin$flow_m3s[abs(as.numeric(allin$date - peak_date)) <= 3])) |>
  ungroup() |>
  transmute(`Peak day` = peak_date, `3-day rain (mm)` = round(total_mm),
            `Max daily rain (mm)` = round(max_day_mm), `Max daily wind (m/s)` = round(max_wind, 1),
            `Peak inflow (m³/s)` = round(peak_q, 1)) |>
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-storm-response
#| tbl-cap: "Lake response to large storms: anomaly (relative to the site-and-month median) of the first integrated sample within 45 days after each of the 40 largest 3-day rain events since 1995, against the anomaly of all other samples."
int <- lw |> filter(layer == "INT", variable %in% c("tp", "drp", "tn", "nnn", "chla", "turb")) |>
  mutate(month = as.integer(format(date, "%m"))) |>
  group_by(site, variable, month) |> mutate(anom = value - median(value)) |> ungroup()
big <- me$storms |> filter(peak_date >= as.Date("1995-01-01")) |> slice_max(total_mm, n = 40)
post <- bind_rows(lapply(big$peak_date, function(d) {
  int |> filter(date > d, date <= d + 45) |>
    group_by(site, variable) |> slice_min(date, n = 1) |> ungroup() |> mutate(storm = d)
}))
resp_tab <- int |>
  mutate(after_storm = paste(site, variable, date) %in% paste(post$site, post$variable, post$date)) |>
  group_by(variable, after_storm) |>
  summarise(n = n(), med_anom = median(anom), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = after_storm, values_from = c(n, med_anom))
wt <- int |>
  mutate(after_storm = paste(site, variable, date) %in% paste(post$site, post$variable, post$date)) |>
  group_by(variable) |>
  summarise(p = tryCatch(wilcox.test(anom[after_storm], anom[!after_storm])$p.value,
                         error = function(e) NA_real_))
resp_tab |> left_join(wt, by = "variable") |>
  transmute(Variable = var_lab[variable], `n after storm` = n_TRUE,
            `Median anomaly after storm` = signif(med_anom_TRUE, 2),
            `Median anomaly otherwise` = signif(med_anom_FALSE, 2), `p (Wilcoxon)` = signif(p, 2)) |>
  kable()
```

**Large storms.**

- The largest storms in the continuous record are:
  - July 2004
  - late July 2025 (285 mm in 3 days)
  - May 2010
  - January 2011
  - Cyclone Gabrielle (13–14 February 2023)
  - April 2017 (two events)
  - March 2016
- **Flows.** Modelled total inflow peaked at 97 m³/s on 29 April 2018 and 83 m³/s on 28 January 2023, the highest since the 1960s.

**Lake response.**

- **No consistent spike.** Monthly sampling seldom catches storm effects. Across 40 large storms, the first sample after a storm was not significantly different in TP, DRP, TN or turbidity. Chl-a was slightly higher (median +1.1 mg/m³, p ≈ 0.05).
- **Lasting effects.** These come through the annual loads and through mixing:
  - The wet years 2011–2013, 2017–2018 and 2023–2024 carried 40–60 t/y of TP and 570–815 t/y of TN (alum_storm_central), well above the PC10 targets.
  - The cool, windy and wet summer of 2022/23 (the Gabrielle summer) had little stratification, well-oxygenated bottom water and the lowest bottom DRP of the decade.
  - The large N load of 2023–2024 is the most likely source of the higher TN and NOx in 2023–2026.

### Case studies

**2009/10 – 2010/11: the last high-internal-load period before full dosing.**

- Long stratification (51 days in summer 2008/09, 46 days in 2010/11) brought repeated anoxia.
- Bottom DRP reached 116 mg/m³ and NH₄ 732 mg/m³ at Site 5 in 2010.
- Full dosing on both streams from 2011 (88–100 t Al/y) was followed by the lowest TP (13–17 mg/m³) and TLI on record in 2012–2013, despite the wet, high-load years 2011–2013.

**2014/15 and 2015/16: hot summers under dosing.**

- 2015 had the 30-day anoxic period, and bottom DRP and NH₄ returned to 56–78 and 490–670 mg/m³.
- Surface TP stayed near 20 mg/m³.
- Internal release persisted under dosing, but was not mixed into the epilimnion in large amounts.

**2019–2022: dosing pause, heat and drought.**

- **Dosing pause.** Puarenga dosing dropped to 6.5 t Al in 2018/19 and to zero in 2019/20, and resumed during 2020/21.
- **Weather.**
  - 2019 was very dry (794 mm), and 2019 and 2020 were warm and sunny.
  - 2020/21 and 2021/22 had the lowest external TP loads since the 1990s (28–29 t/y).
  - Summer 2021/22 brought an air heatwave (21 days, Dec 2021 – Jan 2022), a strong lake heatwave and at least 70 days of stratification (@sec-strat2122).
- **Lake response.**
  - Bottom DRP reached 108–118 mg/m³ and TP 157–162 mg/m³.
  - Surface DRP and TP rose to the highest values since 2010.
- **Reading.** With external loads at a minimum, this points to an internal source. The sediment P was no longer being capped by Puarenga alum, and was then released under strong, long stratification. See @sec-pause for the sequence and why the model misses it.
- **Recovery.** TP fell back in 2022/23, after the resumption of dosing (64 t Al from Puarenga in 2022/23) and in a cool, wet, well-mixed summer (@sec-2023-decline).

**2023 – 2026: wet years, high N loads, rising TN and chl-a.**

- 2023 was the wettest year in the ERA5 record (2478 mm), followed by an above-average 2024.
- The 2023 TN load (814 t/y) was the highest since 1990, and 2024 (706 t/y) was also well above the target.
- Lake TN, NH₄ and NOx rose, and in 2026 chl-a rose and Secchi depth fell.
- TP has stayed near 19–21 mg/m³ under steady dosing (50–96 t Al/y).

### The 2019–2022 phosphorus excursion {#sec-pause}

Lake TP doubled between 2017–2020 and 2021–2022, from about 15 to 27–32 mg/m³ (annual means of the integrated samples). This was the largest change since full dosing began. The evidence below points to internal loading that built up while Puarenga dosing was paused, amplified by the hot, long-stratified summer of 2021/22.

```{r}
#| label: pause-data
p_lo <- as.Date("2016-07-01"); p_hi <- as.Date("2026-07-01")
pz <- pua_pause_main
lag_end <- as.Date("2022-09-30")      # last month of high bottom-water P after dosing resumed
shade <- function() list(
  annotate("rect", xmin = pz$start, xmax = pz$end, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "grey60", alpha = 0.25),
  annotate("rect", xmin = pz$end, xmax = lag_end, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "#E69F00", alpha = 0.12))
lake_mean <- function(v, L) lw |>
  filter(variable == v, layer == L, date >= p_lo, date < p_hi) |>
  group_by(date) |> summarise(value = mean(value), .groups = "drop")
jfm <- lw |>
  filter(layer == "BOT", variable %in% c("drp", "tp"), as.integer(format(date, "%m")) %in% 1:3) |>
  mutate(hy = wq_hy(date)) |>
  group_by(hy, variable) |> summarise(value = mean(value), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(panel = ifelse(variable == "drp", "Bottom DRP, Jan–Mar (mg/m³)", "Bottom TP, Jan–Mar (mg/m³)"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-pause-sequence
#| fig-cap: "Sequence of the 2019–2022 excursion, July 2016 to June 2026. Top: aluminium dosed per month, Puarenga and Utuhina stacked (t Al). March–June 2026 (pale bars) is estimated from the dosed alum volume (about 0.057 kg Al per litre, the median over 2022–2026). Middle: bottom-water (BOT) TP and DRP. Bottom: integrated (INT) TP and DRP. Middle and bottom panels show the mean of Sites 2 and 5 on each sampling date. Grey: Puarenga dosing paused (Sep 2018 – Nov 2020). Orange: the two summers of high bottom-water P after dosing resumed."
#| fig-height: 8
al_m <- alum |>
  filter(date >= p_lo, date < p_hi) |>
  mutate(m = as.Date(format(date, "%Y-%m-15"))) |>
  group_by(m) |> summarise(Puarenga = sum(puarenga_kg_al) / 1000, Utuhina = sum(utuhina_kg_al) / 1000,
                           estimated = any(estimated), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_longer(c(Puarenga, Utuhina), names_to = "stream") |>
  mutate(stream = factor(stream, c("Utuhina", "Puarenga")))   # Puarenga at the bottom of each stack
pa <- ggplot(al_m, aes(m, value, fill = stream, alpha = estimated)) + shade() +
  geom_col(position = "stack", width = 25) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Puarenga = "#0072B2", Utuhina = "#56B4E9"), breaks = c("Puarenga", "Utuhina")) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 1, `TRUE` = 0.45), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "t Al / month", fill = NULL)
pp_fun <- function(L, ttl) {
  d <- bind_rows(lake_mean("tp", L) |> mutate(var = "TP"), lake_mean("drp", L) |> mutate(var = "DRP"))
  ggplot(d, aes(date, value, colour = var)) + shade() +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.4) + geom_point(size = 0.9) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(TP = "#009E73", DRP = "#CC79A7")) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = paste(ttl, "(mg/m³)"), colour = NULL)
}
(pa / pp_fun("BOT", "Bottom") / pp_fun("INT", "Integrated")) &
  scale_x_date(limits = c(p_lo, p_hi), date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") &
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-pause-summers
#| fig-cap: "Summer by summer, hydrological years 2008–2026. Panels: January–March mean bottom-water DRP and TP (both sites); longest buoy-recorded stratified period; external TP load (PC10 2026 loads); and Puarenga aluminium dosed. Orange bars are the pause and recovery years (hy2019–2022). The bottom-water P built up while external loads were at their lowest, and stratification was unusual only in 2021/22. The 2021/22 bar (70 days) is a minimum, because the buoy record has a gap at the end of that period (@sec-strat2122)."
#| fig-height: 8
strat_long <- be$stratified |> mutate(hy = wq_hy(start)) |>
  group_by(hy) |> summarise(value = max(duration), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(panel = "Longest stratified period (days)")
drv <- dla |> transmute(hy, `External TP load (t/y)` = load_tp) |>
  left_join(alum |> mutate(hy = wq_hy(date)) |> group_by(hy) |>
              summarise(`Puarenga Al dosed (t/y)` = sum(puarenga_kg_al) / 1000), by = "hy") |>
  pivot_longer(-hy, names_to = "panel")
sumz <- bind_rows(jfm |> select(hy, panel, value), strat_long, drv) |>
  filter(hy >= 2008, hy <= 2026) |>
  mutate(pause = hy %in% 2019:2022,
         panel = factor(panel, c("Bottom DRP, Jan–Mar (mg/m³)", "Bottom TP, Jan–Mar (mg/m³)",
                                 "Longest stratified period (days)", "External TP load (t/y)",
                                 "Puarenga Al dosed (t/y)")))
ggplot(sumz, aes(hy, value, fill = pause)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey70", `TRUE` = "#D55E00"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2008:2026) +
  labs(x = "Hydrological year (ending June)", y = NULL)
```

**What the data show.**

- **The model's alum input and the dosing record agree.** Puarenga dosing fell to 6.5 t Al in 2018/19, stopped from September 2018 to November 2020, and then resumed (@fig-pause-sequence). Utuhina dosing continued unchanged.
- **Summer bottom-water P built up year on year during the pause.** January–March bottom DRP rose from about 1 mg/m³ (2018) to 8.5 (2019), 22 (2020) and 34 (2021 and 2022). Bottom TP rose from 22 to 37, 43 and about 70 mg/m³ over the same years (@fig-pause-summers).
- **The build-up mixed into the surface.** Each autumn (April–June), when the lake mixes, the bottom-water P spread through the water column. Surface TP reached 39 mg/m³ in early 2021 and 42 mg/m³ in autumn 2022. In winter it fell back to 14–23 mg/m³, but from a higher base each year.
- **It was not driven by external load.** External TP loads in 2020/21 and 2021/22 were the lowest since the 1990s (28–29 t/y, against 40–60 t/y in 2017–2018), and inflow volumes were low.
- **Stratification amplified it, but only at the end.** Summers 2018/19 to 2020/21 were not unusually stratified. Summer 2021/22 had the longest stratified period on record (at least 70 days; @sec-strat2122), an air heatwave, a strong lake heatwave and the warmest December–February air temperature in the record (19.4 °C). It produced the peak bottom-water DRP and TP (108–118 and 157–162 mg/m³).
- **Recovery lagged the restart of dosing by about two summers.** Bottom-water P stayed high in summers 2020/21 and 2021/22, after dosing resumed in November 2020. It fell sharply only from late 2022. That followed heavier dosing (96 t Al in 2022/23) and the cool, wet, well-mixed 2023.
- **2023–2026.** Summer bottom-water P stayed far below the 2021–2022 peak. It rose again in early 2024 and 2025 (single-sample bottom DRP peaks of about 45 and 70 mg/m³), but only briefly. Summer 2025/26 was low (January–March bottom DRP about 5 mg/m³).
- **Autumn 2026.** Integrated TP rose to 33 mg/m³ in March and 40 mg/m³ in April 2026, then fell back to about 19 mg/m³ in May–June. DRP stayed low (1–3 mg/m³) while chl-a reached 30 mg/m³ in April, so the peak was mostly algal (particulate) P, not a return of the internal release seen in 2021–2022.
- **Puarenga dosing stopped again in May 2026.** The 2022–2026 dose-rate workbook shows Puarenga dosing ending in early May 2026, at zero through June and July, while Utuhina dosing continued at a higher rate. If this is a second pause, the 2018–2020 sequence suggests bottom-water P could start to build up within one to two summers.
- **It is not a laboratory artefact.** The finer reporting from 2021 (@sec-dq) affects low DRP values. It cannot produce a doubling of TP, or bottom TP of 70–160 mg/m³.

**Interpretation.**

- **How Puarenga dosing caps the sediment.** The Puarenga is dosed at about 33 mol Al per mol P, far more than is needed to bind the stream's P. The excess aluminium enters the lake as floc and keeps a P-binding layer on the lake bed, where it limits the release of P during low-oxygen periods.
- **What happened when it stopped.** With no fresh floc, the binding capacity aged and was buried over one to two years. Each summer's anoxic release was then less suppressed than the summer before.
- **The 2021/22 peak.** The very long stratification of summer 2021/22 coincided with weakened sediment binding, and produced the peak.
- **The recovery.** It needed the binding layer to rebuild, which took about two summers of renewed dosing.
- **What this implies.** The lake's phosphorus state depends on the continuity of dosing more than on the size of the external load. A break in dosing shows up as rising internal loading within one to two summers.

```{r}
#| label: pause-model
pause_file <- here::here("calibration", "wq_targets", "pause", "sed_ens.rds")
have_pause <- file.exists(pause_file)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-pause-model
#| fig-cap: "The same period in the calibrated model (24-member long ensemble, calibration/all_stage). Left: annual surface TP, observed (integrated samples, black) and modelled (0–8 m mean; line = ensemble median, ribbon = range). Right: modelled sediment indices relative to their 2015–2017 mean: lake-water alum capacity (ALU_ala), sediment alum capacity (ALU_ben_ala), P taken up by sediment alum (ALU_uptake_s) and gross sediment FRP release (PHS_frp_dsf), with the observed January–March bottom DRP (dashed) for comparison. Grey: Puarenga dosing paused."
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| eval: !expr have_pause
se <- readRDS(pause_file)
pause_band <- annotate("rect", xmin = 2018.7, xmax = 2020.9, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "grey60", alpha = 0.25)
tp_m <- se |> filter(var_sim == "PHS_tp_s") |>
  group_by(hy) |> summarise(med = median(v), lo = min(v), hi = max(v), .groups = "drop")
tp_o <- dla |> filter(hy >= 2013, hy <= 2022)
p1 <- ggplot(tp_m, aes(hy)) + pause_band +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "#0072B2", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = med, colour = "Model")) +
  geom_line(data = tp_o, aes(hy, lake_tp, colour = "Observed")) +
  geom_point(data = tp_o, aes(hy, lake_tp, colour = "Observed")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Model = "#0072B2", Observed = "black")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2013:2022) +
  labs(x = "Hydrological year", y = "Surface TP (mg/m³)", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5))
idx_lab <- c(ALU_ala = "Lake-water alum capacity", ALU_ben_ala_Z_lake = "Sediment alum capacity",
             ALU_uptake_s_Z_lake = "P uptake by sediment alum", PHS_frp_dsf_Z_lake = "Sediment FRP release")
obs_lab <- "Observed bottom DRP (Jan–Mar)"
idx <- se |> filter(var_sim %in% names(idx_lab)) |>
  group_by(hy, var_sim) |> summarise(v = median(v), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(var_sim) |> mutate(rel = v / mean(v[hy %in% 2015:2017])) |> ungroup() |>
  mutate(series = unname(idx_lab[var_sim])) |>
  bind_rows(jfm |> filter(variable == "drp", hy >= 2013, hy <= 2022) |>
              mutate(rel = value / mean(value[hy %in% 2015:2017]), series = obs_lab)) |>
  mutate(obs = series == obs_lab)
p2 <- ggplot(idx, aes(hy, rel, colour = series, linetype = obs)) + pause_band +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line() + geom_point(size = 1) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Lake-water alum capacity" = "#56B4E9", "Sediment alum capacity" = "#0072B2",
                                 "P uptake by sediment alum" = "#009E73", "Sediment FRP release" = "#D55E00",
                                 "Observed bottom DRP (Jan–Mar)" = "black")) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 1, `TRUE` = 2), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2013:2022) +
  labs(x = "Hydrological year", y = "Relative to 2015–2017 (log scale)", colour = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5))
p1 + p2 + plot_layout(widths = c(1, 1.4))
```

**Why the model does not reproduce it.**

- **The input is correct.** The calibration inflows contain the pause: Puarenga alum is zero from September 2018 to October 2020. Puarenga inflow FRP rises about fourfold over the pause, because the in-stream reaction no longer removes it.
- **The modelled TP bump is early and short.** It comes from that extra stream FRP and the wet 2017–2018 years, peaking in 2018–2019. It is then flushed out, so all 24 members simulate TP falling by 5–8 mg/m³ from 2017–2020 to 2021–2022, where the lake rose by about 14 (@fig-pause-model).
- **The sediment alum pool reacts too fast.** It loses about 60% of its capacity in the first year of the pause and recovers within a year of dosing restarting. In the lake, the binding loss and the recovery each took about two years.
- **Gross sediment P release is fixed.** It is a constant flux in the model (`aed_sed_const2d`) and changes by only 5–8% across the pause. The model has no store of sediment P whose release grows when the alum binding is lost.

The misfit is therefore structural, and calibrating parameters cannot remove it: the one-stage calibration with this response as a target left it unchanged (z about −8; `calibration/wq_targets/README.md`). The model needs two additions:

- a sediment P pool that accumulates and is released when the binding capacity falls;
- an alum binding capacity in the sediment that decays over one to two years.

The analysis is in `calibration/wq_targets/pause/`.

### Summer 2021/22: the longest recorded stratified period {#sec-strat2122}

The buoy recorded the lake as stratified for 70 days without a break, from 8 November 2021 to 16 January 2022. This is the longest stratified period in the buoy record; the next longest are 52 days (2014/15) and 51 days (2008/09). **70 days is a minimum.** The period does not end with an observed mixing event. It ends because the bottom temperature record stops: the old buoy's last bottom reading is on 16 January, and the new buoy starts on 21 February. This section sets out the data behind the event and what they say about when it ended.

```{r}
#| label: s2122-data
s_from <- as.Date("2021-10-01"); s_to <- as.Date("2022-03-31")
s_ev <- be$stratified |> slice_max(duration, n = 1)                       # 8 Nov 2021 - 16 Jan 2022
s_gap <- tibble(start = as.Date("2022-01-17"), end = as.Date("2022-02-20")) # no buoy bottom temperature
s_d <- be$daily |> filter(date >= s_from, date <= s_to) |>
  tidyr::complete(date = seq(s_from, s_to, by = "day"))   # NA rows so lines break at data gaps
s_in <- s_d |> filter(date >= s_ev$start, date <= s_ev$end)
s_dmax <- s_in |> slice_max(d_temp, n = 1)
s_smax <- s_in |> slice_max(t_surf, n = 1)
s_tb <- range(s_in$t_bot, na.rm = TRUE)
s_ndays <- sum(is_stratified(s_in$d_rho), na.rm = TRUE)
# CTD casts: surface (<= 1.5 m) and bottom (deepest 2 m of each cast), Sites 2 and 5
s_ctd <- ctd |> filter(date >= s_from, date <= s_to, var %in% c("temp_c", "do_mgl")) |>
  group_by(site, date, var) |>
  summarise(top = mean(value[depth_m <= 1.5], na.rm = TRUE),
            bot = mean(value[depth_m >= max(depth_m) - 2], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(across(c(top, bot), \(x) ifelse(is.nan(x), NA_real_, x))) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = var, values_from = c(top, bot)) |>
  mutate(d_temp = top_temp_c - bot_temp_c, d_rho = strat_drho(top_temp_c, bot_temp_c))
# met over the stratified period against the same calendar days in other years
s_met <- me$daily |> mutate(doy = as.integer(format(date, "%j")), y = as.integer(format(date, "%Y")),
                           hy = ifelse(doy >= 312, y + 1L, y)) |>
  filter(doy >= 312 | doy <= 16, hy >= 1977, hy <= 2026) |>
  group_by(hy) |> summarise(tair = mean(tair), wind = mean(wind), rain = sum(rain_mm), .groups = "drop")
s_met22 <- s_met |> filter(hy == 2022)
s_clim <- s_met |> filter(hy %in% 1991:2020) |> summarise(tair = mean(tair), wind = mean(wind))
s_rank_t <- rank(-s_met$tair)[s_met$hy == 2022]; s_rank_w <- rank(s_met$wind)[s_met$hy == 2022]
# bottom-water chemistry, mean of Sites 2 and 5
s_bot <- lw |> filter(layer == "BOT", date >= as.Date("2021-09-01"), date <= as.Date("2022-06-30")) |>
  group_by(date, variable) |> summarise(value = mean(value), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = value)
s_b1117 <- s_bot |> filter(date == as.Date("2021-11-17")); s_b1220 <- s_bot |> filter(date == as.Date("2021-12-20"))
s_rate <- function(v) (s_b1220[[v]] - s_b1117[[v]]) / as.numeric(s_b1220$date - s_b1117$date)
s_band <- function(ev, fill, alpha = 0.35) geom_rect(data = ev, aes(xmin = start - 0.5, xmax = end + 0.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
                                               inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = fill, alpha = alpha)
s_bands <- function() list(s_band(s_ev, "grey70", 0.3), s_band(s_gap, "#FDDBC7", 0.6))
s_x <- scale_x_date(limits = c(s_from, s_to), date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b\n%Y", expand = c(0, 0))
s_ctd_dates <- sort(unique(s_ctd$date))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-s2122-overview
#| fig-cap: "Summer 2021/22, October 2021 to March 2022. (a) Buoy water temperature by depth (old buoy to 18 January 2022, new buoy from 21 February); dashed lines are the CTD sampling dates. (b) Buoy surface (≤ 1.5 m) and bottom (≥ 18 m) temperature (lines), with the CTD surface and bottom temperatures at Sites 2 and 5 (points). (c) Bottom − surface density difference; the dotted line is the 0.2 kg/m³ stratification threshold. (d) Bottom DO from the buoys (line; the old buoy's 20 m sensor stopped on 14 November) and the bottom of each CTD cast (points); the dashed line is 2 g/m³. (e) ERA5-BC daily air temperature (black) and wind speed (grey), with air heatwaves (red) and storms (blue). Grey band: the 70-day buoy-recorded stratified period. Orange band: no buoy bottom temperature (17 January – 20 February)."
#| fig-height: 11
s_heat <- bpl |> filter(date >= s_from, date <= s_to, is.finite(temp_c)) |>
  arrange(source, date, depth_m) |> group_by(source, date) |>
  mutate(top = (depth_m + lag(depth_m, default = 0)) / 2, bot = (depth_m + lead(depth_m, default = max(depth_m) + 0.25)) / 2) |>
  ungroup()   # each sensor fills the depth range half-way to its neighbours (old buoy: about 2 m apart)
pa <- ggplot(s_heat, aes(fill = temp_c)) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = date - 0.5, xmax = date + 0.5, ymin = top, ymax = bot)) +
  s_band(s_gap, "white", 1) +
  annotate("text", x = s_gap$start + 17, y = 10, label = "no buoy data", size = 3, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = s_ctd_dates, linetype = 2, colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_y_reverse() + scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "inferno", name = "°C") +
  s_x + labs(x = NULL, y = "Depth (m)", tag = "a")
pb <- s_d |> select(date, Surface = t_surf, Bottom = t_bot) |> pivot_longer(-date) |>
  ggplot(aes(date, value, colour = name)) + s_bands() +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(data = s_ctd |> select(site, date, Surface = top_temp_c, Bottom = bot_temp_c) |> pivot_longer(Surface:Bottom),
             aes(shape = site), size = 2, show.legend = c(colour = FALSE, shape = TRUE)) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = NA))) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Surface = "#D55E00", Bottom = "#0072B2")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Site 2" = 16, "Site 5" = 17)) +
  s_x + labs(x = NULL, y = "Water temp (°C)", colour = NULL, shape = "CTD", tag = "b")
pc <- ggplot(s_d, aes(date, d_rho)) + s_bands() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = strat_drho_threshold(), linetype = 3) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.4) + geom_point(size = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = s_ctd, aes(shape = site), size = 2) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Site 2" = 16, "Site 5" = 17)) +
  s_x + labs(x = NULL, y = "Δρ bottom − surface (kg/m³)", shape = "CTD", tag = "c")
pd <- ggplot(s_d, aes(date, do_bot)) + s_bands() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 2, linetype = 2, colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_line(colour = "purple4", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(data = s_ctd |> filter(is.finite(bot_do_mgl)), aes(y = bot_do_mgl, shape = site), size = 2) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Site 2" = 16, "Site 5" = 17)) +
  s_x + labs(x = NULL, y = "Bottom DO (g/m³)", shape = "CTD", tag = "d")
s_md <- me$daily |> filter(date >= s_from, date <= s_to)
pe <- ggplot(s_md, aes(date)) +
  s_band(me$air_heatwaves |> filter(end >= s_from, start <= s_to), "#F4A582", 0.5) +
  s_band(me$storms |> filter(end >= s_from, start <= s_to), "#92C5DE", 0.7) +
  geom_line(aes(y = tair), colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_line(aes(y = wind * 2), colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_y_continuous(sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / 2, name = "Wind (m/s, grey)")) +
  s_x + labs(x = NULL, y = "Air temp (°C, black)", tag = "e")
(pa / pb / pc / pd / pe) + plot_layout(heights = c(1.3, 1, 0.8, 0.8, 0.8), guides = "collect")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-s2122-ctd
#| fig-cap: "CTD profiles of temperature and DO at Sites 2 and 5, October 2021 to March 2022. DO was not recorded at Site 2 on 17 November and 16 February, and at Site 5 there was no November cast."
#| fig-height: 6.5
s_prof <- ctd |> filter(date >= as.Date("2021-10-15"), date <= s_to, var %in% c("temp_c", "do_mgl")) |>
  mutate(var = factor(var, c("temp_c", "do_mgl"), c("Temperature (°C)", "DO (g/m³)")),
         cast = factor(format(date, "%d %b %Y"), format(sort(unique(date)), "%d %b %Y")))
ggplot(s_prof, aes(value, depth_m, colour = cast)) +
  geom_path(linewidth = 0.6) +

```

```{r}
#| label: fig-s2122-chem
#| fig-cap: "Nutrients and chl-a in the integrated (INT, 0–6 m), hypolimnion (HYP; 15 m at Site 2, 18 m at Site 5) and bottom (BOT) samples, September 2021 to June 2022. Grey band: the 70-day buoy-recorded stratified period; orange band: no buoy bottom temperature."
#| fig-height: 9
s_chem <- lw |> filter(date >= as.Date("2021-09-01"), date <= as.Date("2022-06-30"),
                       variable %in% c("nh4", "drp", "tp", "tn", "nnn", "chla")) |>
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, c("nh4", "drp", "tp", "tn", "nnn", "chla"), var_lab[c("nh4", "drp", "tp", "tn", "nnn", "chla")]))
ggplot(s_chem, aes(date, value, colour = layer)) + s_bands() +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.4) + geom_point(size = 1.4) +
  facet_grid(variable ~ site, scales = "free_y", switch = "y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_layer) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 months", date_labels = "%b\n%Y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme(strip.placement = "outside", strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 90))
```

**Weather.** The stratified period was the warmest on record for those calendar days, and among the calmest.

- Over 8 November – 16 January, ERA5-BC air temperature averaged `r sprintf("%.1f", s_met22$tair)` °C. That is `r sprintf("%.1f", s_met22$tair - s_clim$tair)` °C above the 1991–2020 mean, and the warmest of the `r nrow(s_met)` years in the record (@fig-s2122-overview e).
- Mean wind was `r sprintf("%.1f", s_met22$wind)` m/s against `r sprintf("%.1f", s_clim$wind)` m/s normally, the `r scales::ordinal(s_rank_w)` calmest of `r nrow(s_met)` years. There were no storms during the period.
- It included two air heatwaves: 7–16 November (Moderate) and 22 December – 11 January (Strong, 21 days). There were also two lake surface heatwaves: 23 November – 2 December and 25 December – 12 January (Strong, 19 days).

**Onset (early November).**

- The lake was stratifying and mixing intermittently through late October. A mixing spell on 3–7 November brought the surface–bottom difference back to near zero.
- Stratification then set in on 8 November, during the first air heatwave, and did not break again in the buoy record (@fig-s2122-overview b, c).

**The stratified period (8 November – 16 January).**

- The lake was stratified (density difference above 0.2 kg/m³) on all `r s_ndays` days with data. The 2 days without data (20 December, and 15 January for the bottom sensor) are bridged by the 2-day gap rule (@sec-event-defs).
- The difference peaked at `r sprintf("%.1f", s_dmax$d_temp)` °C on `r format(s_dmax$date, "%d %B")`. The surface reached `r sprintf("%.1f", s_smax$t_surf)` °C on `r format(s_smax$date, "%d %B")`, during the lake heatwave.
- The thermocline moved deeper as the period went on. On 17 November it sat at about 17–20 m at Site 2. By 20 December the temperature gradient spread from about 13 to 21 m at Site 2 and from 16 to 20 m at Site 5 (@fig-s2122-ctd).
- The bottom water still warmed steadily, from `r sprintf("%.1f", s_tb[1])` to `r sprintf("%.1f", s_tb[2])` °C. Heat continued to reach it by mixing across the thermocline, so the deep water was not fully isolated.
- The buoy's bottom-DO record does not cover the anoxia. Bottom DO at 20 m was falling from about 8.6 to 6.8 g/m³ in the first week, then the sensor stopped on 14 November.
- **The CTD casts show it instead** (@fig-s2122-ctd).
  - On 20 December, bottom DO was 0.3–0.5 g/m³ at both sites. DO was below 2 g/m³ only in the deepest 2–5 m (below 20 m at Site 5 and 22 m at Site 2).
  - That thin anoxic layer explains why the bottom (BOT) samples are far more enriched than the hypolimnion (HYP) samples a few metres higher.

**Nutrients during the stratified period** (@fig-s2122-chem).

- On 17 November, about 10 days into the period, bottom NH₄ had already risen to about `r round(s_b1117$nh4)` mg/m³, while DRP was still low (about `r round(s_b1117$drp)` mg/m³).
- By 20 December (mean of the two sites):
  - bottom TP was `r round(s_b1220$tp)` mg/m³;
  - DRP `r round(s_b1220$drp)` mg/m³;
  - NH₄ `r round(s_b1220$nh4)` mg/m³;
  - TN `r round(s_b1220$tn)` mg/m³.
- These are the highest bottom-water P concentrations since 2010.
- Between the two sampling dates, bottom NH₄ rose by about `r round(s_rate("nh4"))` mg/m³/d and DRP by about `r sprintf("%.1f", s_rate("drp"))` mg/m³/d.
- Bottom NOx fell from about 42 to 13 mg/m³ and then to about 1.5 mg/m³ by January, which is consistent with denitrification in the anoxic layer.
- Surface (INT) DRP stayed at 2–3 mg/m³ until December. Chl-a was high (20–22 mg/m³) in November and December.

**The end of the stratified period (between 16 January and 16 February).** No buoy data cover the end, but the CTD casts bracket it.

- **Mid-January.** The surface–bottom difference fell after the lake heatwave peak:
  - 4.6 °C on 6 January;
  - 2.6–2.9 °C on 9–14 January, a windier spell with daily mean wind of 7–7.7 m/s on several days;
  - 1.4 °C on 16 January, the last day with a bottom reading.
- **19 January (CTD).** The lake was only weakly stratified: surface − bottom 1.1–1.2 °C, a density difference of about 0.27 kg/m³, just above the threshold (@fig-s2122-overview c).
  - Bottom DO had recovered to 4.0–4.8 g/m³, so the anoxic layer had already been partly reoxygenated.
  - DO between 5 and 15 m had fallen from about 8.5 g/m³ in December to 4–7 g/m³. DO was 4–7 g/m³ through the whole water column, which is consistent with the low-oxygen bottom water having been mixed upwards.
  - Bottom DRP (73–78 mg/m³) and NH₄ (370–400 mg/m³) were still high.
  - Surface DRP had risen to 9.6 mg/m³ at both sites, the first sign of bottom water mixing into the surface.
- **16 February (CTD).** The lake was mixed (surface − bottom ≤ 0.4 °C, a density difference below 0.1 kg/m³), and bottom DO was 6.3 g/m³ at Site 5.
  - This followed the storm of 7 February (195 mm in one day) and a windy 13 February (11 m/s).
  - Bottom DRP had fallen to about 16 mg/m³. Surface TP had risen to 38–40 mg/m³ and surface NH₄ to 19–44 mg/m³.
- **From 21 February (new buoy).** The water column was close to uniform at 21.7–22.5 °C, with only brief, weak stratification.

**What this means for the duration.**

- The stratified period lasted at least 70 days.
- It cannot have lasted beyond 16 February, when the CTD casts show the lake mixed. That gives an upper limit of about 100 days.
- The falling temperature difference in mid-January and the partly reoxygenated bottom water on 19 January suggest the stratification was already breaking down in the second half of January. The true duration was therefore probably closer to 70–80 days than to 100.

**Where the released nutrients went.**

- The P and N released in December did not stay in the bottom water.
- Once the lake mixed, surface TP rose from 27–29 mg/m³ in December–January to 38–40 mg/m³ in February and 47–50 mg/m³ in March. These were the highest surface values since 2010.
- Chl-a rose again to 17–19 mg/m³ in March.
- Surface TP stayed near 40 mg/m³ until June. This is the 2021/22 peak of the excursion in @sec-pause.

### 2022–2023: phosphorus drawn down across the lake {#sec-2023-decline}

After the 2021–2022 peak (@sec-pause), lake TP and DRP fell to some of the lowest values of the alum era and stayed low through 2023. This section asks what drew the phosphorus down: the larger alum dose in the Puarenga, flushing by the very wet 2023, or the lack of summer internal loading.

```{r}
#| label: d23-data
d_lo <- as.Date("2020-07-01"); d_hi <- as.Date("2024-07-01")
lake_vol_m3 <- sum(diff(hyps$depth) * (head(hyps$area, -1) + tail(hyps$area, -1)) / 2)   # about 830 Mm3
mo_of <- function(d) as.Date(format(d, "%Y-%m-15"))
d_flow <- pflow |>
  filter(inflow %in% c("All inflows", "Ohau outflow", "Puarenga", "Utuhina"), date >= d_lo, date < d_hi) |>
  mutate(mo = mo_of(date)) |> group_by(mo, inflow) |>
  summarise(vol = sum(flow_m3s) * 86400 / 1e6, .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = inflow, values_from = vol) |>
  rename(inflow = `All inflows`, outflow = `Ohau outflow`, q_pua = Puarenga, q_utu = Utuhina)
d_load <- sl |> group_by(hy) |> summarise(load_tp = sum(tp), .groups = "drop")
d_tp <- lw |> filter(layer == "INT", variable %in% c("tp", "drp"), date >= d_lo, date < d_hi) |>
  mutate(mo = mo_of(date)) |> group_by(mo, variable) |> summarise(v = mean(value), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = v)
d_al <- alum |> filter(date >= d_lo, date < d_hi) |> mutate(mo = mo_of(date)) |> group_by(mo) |>
  summarise(Puarenga = sum(puarenga_kg_al) / 1000, Utuhina = sum(utuhina_kg_al) / 1000, estimated = any(estimated), .groups = "drop")
# monthly TP budget: annual PC10 load spread by monthly inflow; export = outflow x integrated TP; lake mass = TP x volume
d_m <- d_flow |> mutate(hy = wq_hy(mo)) |> group_by(hy) |> mutate(share = inflow / sum(inflow)) |> ungroup() |>
  left_join(d_load, by = "hy") |> mutate(load_t = load_tp * share) |>
  left_join(d_tp, by = "mo") |> left_join(d_al, by = "mo") |> arrange(mo) |>
  mutate(mass_t = tp * lake_vol_m3 / 1e9, export_t = outflow * tp / 1000,
         pua_mgL = Puarenga / q_pua, utu_mgL = Utuhina / q_utu)
budget <- function(from, to) {
  w <- d_m |> filter(mo >= as.Date(from), mo <= as.Date(to), is.finite(mass_t))
  dm <- tail(w$mass_t, 1) - w$mass_t[1]; ld <- sum(w$load_t[-1]); ex <- sum(w$export_t[-1])
  tibble(Period = paste(format(as.Date(from), "%b %Y"), "–", format(as.Date(to), "%b %Y")),
         `Change in lake TP (t)` = dm, `Inflow load (t)` = ld, `Outflow export (t)` = ex, `Net retained in sediment (t)` = ld - ex - dm)
}
d_bud <- bind_rows(budget("2021-05-15", "2022-01-15"), budget("2022-05-15", "2023-01-15"), budget("2023-05-15", "2024-01-15"))
```

(c) Total inflow (modelled, PC10 loads) and Ohau outflow (measured; the recorded Ohau Channel flow), Mm³ per month. (d) Lake TP budget: lake TP mass (integrated TP × lake volume), and the inflow load (modelled) and outflow export (measured flow × integrated TP) accumulated from July 2020.   ggplot(aes(mo, value)) + d_band +

g4 <- d_m |> filter(is.finite(mass_t)) |>

(g1 / g2 / g3 / g4) & theme(legend.position = "right")
